hook: I organized my garage wall for $91, not $2,000

scenes.visual_prompt: Panning shot across a cluttered garage floor: bins stacked three high on a collapsed shelf, a rake and two brooms leaning at odd angles, a coffee can of loose screws
scenes.on_screen_text: My garage before: $0 spent, 0 things findable
scenes.voiceover: This was my garage two weeks ago.

scenes.visual_prompt: Hand pointing up at bare, empty wall space above the 4-foot line
scenes.voiceover: A slatwall installer wanted $2,000. I used the wall space instead.

scenes.visual_prompt: Mounting floating shelves to the wall with a stud finder and drill, three shelves going up at staggered heights
scenes.voiceover: Three shelf sets, twenty minutes, no sagging.

scenes.visual_prompt: Loading uniform clear plastic bins onto the mounted shelves, contents visible through the lids
scenes.voiceover: Every bin looks the same now, and every bin is labeled by what's inside.

scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of a hand spinning a lazy Susan turntable loaded with paint cans on the shelf
scenes.voiceover: No more moving six things to find one.

scenes.visual_prompt: Mounting a key holder with hooks and a small shelf next to the garage door, hanging keys on it
scenes.voiceover: This is the piece that keeps the whole system from backsliding.

scenes.visual_prompt: Wide reveal shot of the finished garage wall — shelves, bins, turntables, key holder, empty floor
scenes.on_screen_text: Total: $90.96. Full breakdown on the blog.

caption: I stopped tripping over garage clutter for $90.96 — not $2,000 for a slatwall installer. Full parts list, prices, and review data on the blog (link in bio).
